title: Google’s Computer Use tool is generally available, and the check for hidden instructions in a screenshot stays off unless you turn it on. DoorDash says outside AI agents have produced several hundred orders, against 993 million in the quarter. A shared robots.txt line can refuse AI training, and the clocks run into 2027. Blackstone expects Anthropic to come out of its IPO with a high junk rating. A tampered Claude Code extension sat in Cursor’s marketplace for hours and tried to leave a backdoor.
summary: On 30 October 2026 Google marked the Gemini API Computer Use tool generally available on the Interactions and GenerateContent APIs. The same documentation says screenshot prompt-injection detection is opt-in and that the default is false. On DoorDash’s 29 October earnings call, chief executive Tony Xu said third-party AI agents have produced several hundred orders across the time they have been running. The company’s 30 October release said third-quarter orders were 993 million, up 28% year over year. The same day OpenAI, Google and Microsoft said they will honor a shared robots.txt token for AI training, on different dates, and an IETF draft named the token __usage_ai-training. TechCrunch, citing the Financial Times, said Blackstone expects Anthropic to receive a high junk rating after its IPO. Microsoft published an analysis of a tampered Claude Code extension that Cursor says was in its marketplace for hours on 29 October.
uncertainty: The general-availability line is the Gemini API changelog for 30 October. The default of false, the model list, and the safety categories are from the Computer Use documentation, which says the injection check applies to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite or later. The public preview date in that changelog is 24 June 2026. DoorDash’s “several hundred” and “maybe several hundred” are Tony Xu’s words on the 29 October call, filed with the SEC, not a precise count and not a share of the quarter. The 993 million, the 28% and the 17% excluding Deliveroo are from the 30 October earnings release. They are different counts. This briefing does not divide them. The robots.txt token, the rule that a User-Agent star group does not count, and the 3 May 2027 expiry are from Kevin Kelley’s individual Internet-Draft of 30 October, which says it is work in progress and not an IETF standard. OpenAI’s “coming months,” Google’s “2027,” and Microsoft’s 1 February 2027 and 1 March 2027 are each company’s own post. The Verge reported that Anthropic has already adopted the signal. This briefing did not find a separate Anthropic post that says so. The Anthropic rating is TechCrunch’s account of a Financial Times report. TechCrunch says Anthropic and Blackstone declined to comment. It is an expectation of a double-B range, not a rating published by S&P, Moody’s or Fitch. The $63 billion is the chip-financing deal TechCrunch describes, not cash raised on 30 October. The extension window, 2:27am to 1:35pm PT on 29 October, and the versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 are Cursor’s. Microsoft’s analysis is dated 30 October. Cursor says the tunnel step fails without administrator rights on most hosts, and that the key and the persistence can still be written.

stories.theme: Google’s Computer Use tool is generally available, and the screenshot injection check stays off unless you turn it on
stories.changed: On Friday 30 October 2026 the Gemini API changelog said Google released the Computer Use tool to general availability across the Interactions API and the GenerateContent API. The same changelog dates the public preview to 24 June 2026, on Gemini 3.5 Flash. The tool lets a model look at a screenshot and return the next click, keystroke or scroll. Your own code has to carry the action out. The documentation lists four models: Gemini 4 Argon, which it calls the most capable, Gemini 3.8 Flash, which it recommends, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, and Gemini 3 Flash Preview. It supports browser, mobile and desktop. Gemini 4 and Gemini 3.x include built-in safety categories that can ask for a person’s confirmation, covering payments, sensitive records, sending messages, creating accounts, changing or deleting data, cookie banners and legal terms. You can switch selected categories off. A separate check looks for hidden instructions in a screenshot, such as “Ignore previous commands,” and blocks the step when it finds them. The documentation says that check is for Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite or later, that it is opt-in, and that the default is false. Google also says the tool may contain errors and security vulnerabilities, and that you should supervise it closely and keep it off tasks that involve critical decisions, sensitive data, or actions that cannot be undone.
stories.matters: A computer-use agent can now be called as a supported API, and the check that reads the screen for hidden instructions is off until you turn it on.
stories.imply: If a pilot was waiting on the preview label, the label has changed. Turn the screenshot check on before the agent reads mail, tickets or the open web. Keep a person on anything that spends money or cannot be undone.
uses: Treat 30 October as the day Computer Use left preview. The model still returns an action. Your application still has to perform it.
Set prompt-injection detection on for any agent whose screenshots include pages, inboxes or documents you do not control. The documented default is false.
Leave the built-in categories on for payments, messages, new accounts and legal agreements unless you have a reason to disable one, and still handle a confirmation the model asks for.
stories.example: A support team wants an agent to update a ticket from a screenshot of a customer’s email. Before the pilot, they turn screenshot injection detection on, leave the message-sending category in place, and keep a person on any step that would reply to the customer.
stories.audience: Teams building or buying an agent that clicks through a browser, a phone or a desktop.
stories.watch: Whether Google changes the default. Which of the four named models your account can actually call. How often a real inbox still gets an action through with the check switched on.

source.title: Gemini API changelog: Computer Use generally available, 30 October 2026
source.quote: Released the Computer Use tool to general availability (GA) across the Interactions and GenerateContent APIs.

stories.theme: DoorDash says outside AI agents have produced several hundred orders, against 993 million in the quarter
stories.changed: On Thursday 29 October 2026, on DoorDash’s third-quarter earnings call, chief executive Tony Xu answered a question about AI agents. He said: “if you look at where AI agents are today, we’re seeing maybe several hundred orders in total from some of these third-party agents.” Later on the same call he said: “right now, AI agents are generating several hundred orders across the time that they’ve been up and running. So it’s been a fairly low use case.” He said everyday food orders still come through the DoorDash app, and that he sees more room for agents on long decisions and on tasks a person is not actively making. DoorDash’s own letter, published with the results, says the company recently shipped Ask DoorDash, Text DoorDash, and a Model Context Protocol connector for external agents, including corporate lunch orders. The 30 October earnings release says total orders rose 28% year over year to 993 million. Excluding the Deliveroo acquisition, total orders rose 17%. Xu’s “several hundred” is about third-party agents, over the whole time they have been running. It is not a figure for the quarter, and it is not a precise count.
stories.matters: A company that completes hundreds of millions of orders a quarter is saying outside agents have barely placed any. The two numbers are not a rate.
stories.imply: Do not put “agents will take the order” into a forecast until you have your own count. “Several hundred” is a description, not a number you can divide into 993 million.
uses: If a vendor says agents are already ordering for your customers, ask for the count and the period. DoorDash’s figure is “several hundred,” across the whole time, not for one quarter.
Keep DoorDash’s own tools separate. Ask DoorDash, Text DoorDash and the corporate connector are not the third-party total Xu gave.
Use 993 million, 28% and 17% only as the quarter’s order totals. Do not turn them into a share of agent orders.
stories.example: A retailer’s partnerships lead stops a slide that says “agent checkout is here.” She writes that DoorDash described several hundred third-party orders in total, against 993 million orders in the quarter, and that the company has not published a precise agent count.
stories.audience: Anyone forecasting that an assistant will place orders, book, or buy on a customer’s behalf.
stories.watch: Whether DoorDash ever replaces “several hundred” with a count. How its own Ask, text and connector volumes compare with outside agents. Whether a simple order stays in the app while longer decisions move.

source.title: DoorDash Q3 2026 earnings call, 29 October 2026, filed with the SEC

stories.theme: One robots.txt line can refuse AI training, and most of the companies say they will not honor it until 2027
stories.changed: On Friday 30 October 2026 OpenAI said it will honor a common signal in robots.txt for whether a site’s content may be used to train foundation generative models. It said the signal will not replace the crawler controls it already has, and that it aims to implement it in the coming months. The same day Google said it plans to support a shared policy token in robots.txt, and that it aims to do so, with other providers, in 2027. If a site uses the token to opt out and does not mention Google-Extended, Google plans to treat that as a disallow of Google-Extended, its own training control since 2023. A site that specifically allows Google-Extended stays eligible to appear in Gemini app answers. Microsoft, the same day, said it will honor the new training and grounding preferences as it crawls, starting 1 February 2027. Training can be set in robots.txt or on a page. Grounding, which Microsoft describes as using a page to inform a generated answer, is a separate page-level setting: allow, disallow, or DisallowExtended, which limits grounding to Microsoft’s own products such as Copilot and Microsoft 365. Both default to allow. Bing search eligibility does not change. Microsoft says neither choice guarantees inclusion, traffic or payment. Sites that use NoArchive or NoCache are asked to publish the new preferences before 1 March 2027, after which those tags will no longer be read as a training or grounding preference. The token itself is in an individual Internet-Draft submitted the same day by Kevin Kelley, who gives his affiliation as Anthropic. The token is __usage_ai-training, written on the User-Agent line. A disallow on that group is a preference against using the path to modify the learned parameters of a generative model. The draft says a User-Agent star group must not be read as this preference, that a file with no line for the token expresses no preference, and that the token is not a directive for crawling. The draft expires on 3 May 2027 and says it is work in progress, not an IETF standard. The Verge reported that Anthropic has already adopted the signal, and that Meta’s communications head welcomed a common signal without saying Meta will honor it. This briefing did not find a separate Anthropic post that confirms the crawler honors the token today.
stories.matters: Publishers may get one line instead of a list of crawler names. Writing it today does not switch the large crawlers off on a shared date.
stories.imply: Keep the crawler rules you already have. Add the token if you want the preference on file. Do not delete GPTBot or Google-Extended and expect the new line to be live.
uses: If you want to refuse training, add a robots.txt group whose User-Agent is __usage_ai-training. A star rule does not count, and an ordinary crawl block is a separate decision.
Write down three clocks: OpenAI says the coming months, Google says 2027, Microsoft says 1 February 2027 for the new preferences and 1 March 2027 for the old NoArchive and NoCache tags.
Decide training and grounding separately. Microsoft’s post says a training refusal does not by itself keep a page out of an answer, and Google’s post ties Gemini grounding to Google-Extended.
stories.example: A publisher’s web lead adds the token, leaves the existing GPTBot and Google-Extended lines in place, and puts 1 February 2027 and “coming months” on the ticket so nobody tells the newsroom the opt-out is already in force.
stories.audience: Publishers, shops and anyone else who already maintains a robots.txt file, and the lawyers who have been asked for one rule that covers every model company.
stories.watch: When OpenAI says the signal is actually on. Whether Google names a day inside 2027. Whether Anthropic publishes its own implementation note. Whether the draft changes before 3 May 2027.

source.title: OpenAI: Making it easier for websites to express AI training preferences, 30 October 2026
source.quote: We aim to implement the signal in the coming months, and will share another update with details about our implementation when we do so.

stories.theme: Blackstone expects Anthropic to come out of its IPO with a high junk rating
stories.changed: On Friday 30 October 2026 TechCrunch reported, citing the Financial Times, that Blackstone expects Anthropic to receive a high junk rating from credit agencies after its initial public offering. TechCrunch says Blackstone is the anchor investor in a recent $63 billion deal to finance Anthropic’s chips, and that Blackstone told investors in that deal it expects the rating. TechCrunch says Blackstone had previously said the opposite: that Anthropic would receive an investment-grade rating before 2027. It now expects a double-B rating, which TechCrunch calls the top tier of speculative junk grade. TechCrunch reached out to Anthropic and Blackstone, and both declined to comment. TechCrunch says the forecast is a prediction, and that a junk rating would make it more difficult and more expensive for Anthropic to raise money for its spending. Anthropic filed to go public earlier in the week. The article does not say that S&P, Moody’s or Fitch has published a rating for the company.
stories.matters: The new fact is a lender’s change of mind about the rating, told to investors in a chip deal. It is not a rating on the screen, and it is not a new model.
stories.imply: If a note says Anthropic will borrow at an investment-grade rate after the listing, that is no longer what Blackstone is reported to be telling its investors. Say “expects,” and say who declined to comment.
uses: Separate three things: the IPO filing already public, the $63 billion chip deal TechCrunch describes, and a reported expectation of a double-B rating.
Do not write that the agencies have rated Anthropic. TechCrunch’s account is Blackstone’s expectation, via the Financial Times, and both companies declined to comment.
If you are modelling Anthropic’s cost of debt, label this as a forecast that can move, not as a coupon.
stories.example: A finance partner rewrites a line that said Anthropic’s debt would be investment grade before 2027. The new line says Blackstone is reported to expect a double-B rating after the IPO, that the companies declined to comment, and that the big agencies are not quoted as having published a rating.
stories.audience: Anyone who lends to, buys from, or models the cost of capital of a frontier lab that is about to list.
stories.watch: Whether S&P, Moody’s or Fitch publish a rating. Whether Blackstone corrects the account. How much of the $63 billion deal has actually been placed.

source.title: TechCrunch, citing the Financial Times: Anthropic expected to receive a high junk rating after its IPO, 30 October 2026

stories.theme: A tampered Claude Code extension sat in Cursor’s marketplace for hours and tried to leave a backdoor
stories.changed: On Thursday 29 October 2026 Cursor said a maliciously modified copy of the Claude Code extension, anthropic.claude-code versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313, for Windows and macOS, was available in the Cursor extension marketplace from about 2:27am to 1:35pm Pacific time. Cursor says those versions were not developed by Anthropic, and that the incident does not affect other extensions from that marketplace. The extension tries to install a persistent SSH backdoor. Cursor says it collects host and user details, tries to add an attacker-controlled SSH key, tries to turn on the local SSH service, and tries to open a reverse tunnel. Cursor says that on most macOS and Windows machines the extension does not have administrator rights, so turning SSH on fails, and that errors in the malicious code mean the tunnel step would fail unless Cursor had been started with those rights. Cursor also says the extension still added the attacker’s key, installed persistence, and sent host details, and that uninstalling may not be enough because the payload leaves scripts that keep running. Cursor says the attacker’s server was taken offline. On Friday 30 October Cursor updated the indicators and clarified the versions. The same day Microsoft published its own analysis. Microsoft says the packages were not on the Visual Studio Marketplace or on npm, that Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised and that it did not develop the package, and that the evidence points to the Cursor marketplace only. Microsoft says the loader may still write the key and the persistence even when the tunnel fails, and that a callback sent names of environment variables, not their values. This is a different incident from the relay that changes the settings of the real Codex and Claude Code command-line tools.
stories.matters: The copy in the marketplace was not Anthropic’s, it was only up for part of a day, and removing the extension does not by itself remove what it already wrote.
stories.imply: Check the version and the install time before you assume a developer machine is clean. A machine that never installed those two versions from that marketplace is outside the window Cursor describes.
uses: On macOS and Windows, look for anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 installed from the Cursor marketplace between 2:27am and 1:35pm Pacific on 29 October.

If a machine is in that window, follow Cursor’s remediation. Cursor says uninstalling can leave persistence behind, and that credentials reachable from the machine should be rotated from a trusted system.
Do not fold this into the earlier report of a relay that turns the sandbox off. That was a changed configuration of the real tools. This was a tampered extension in one marketplace.
stories.example: An IT lead searches the developer fleet for those two extension versions. Two laptops match the window. She takes them off the network, runs Cursor’s cleanup, and has the owners rotate keys from a machine that was not in the window.
stories.audience: Security and IT teams who allow Cursor, and developers who install extensions from its marketplace.
stories.watch: Whether Cursor or Microsoft revise the window or the versions. Whether the same package shows up in another marketplace. Whether Anthropic publishes its own note.

source.title: Microsoft Security: a malicious Claude Code-branded extension in the Cursor marketplace, 30 October 2026
source.quote: Anthropic confirmed to Microsoft that their systems were not compromised and they did not develop the malicious package posted in Cursor marketplace.

signals.raw: Gemini API changelog, 30 Oct: Computer Use generally available on the Interactions and GenerateContent APIs. Docs: models are Gemini 4 Argon, 3.8 Flash (recommended), 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3 Flash Preview. Screenshot prompt-injection detection is opt-in for 3.5 Flash-Lite or later. The default is false. Preview was 24 June 2026.

DoorDash earnings call, 29 Oct, SEC filing: Tony Xu says maybe several hundred orders in total from third-party agents, across the time they have been running, a fairly low use case. Earnings release, 30 Oct: total orders 993 million, up 28% year over year, 17% excluding Deliveroo.

30 Oct: OpenAI will honor a shared robots.txt training signal in the coming months. Google aims to support it in 2027. Microsoft starts 1 February 2027; NoArchive and NoCache stop counting for training and grounding on 1 March 2027. IETF draft the same day names the token __usage_ai-training, says a star rule does not count, and expires 3 May 2027. The Verge says Anthropic has already adopted it.

TechCrunch, 30 Oct, citing the Financial Times: Blackstone expects Anthropic to receive a high junk, double-B rating after the IPO, reversing earlier guidance of investment grade before 2027. Anchor investor in a $63 billion chip deal. Anthropic and Blackstone declined to comment.

Cursor, 29 Oct, updated 30 Oct: anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 on the Cursor marketplace, about 2:27am to 1:35pm PT, not developed by Anthropic. Tries an SSH backdoor. Tunnel step fails without admin on most hosts. Key and persistence can still be written. Uninstalling may not be enough. Microsoft, 30 Oct: not on the Visual Studio Marketplace or npm. Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised.
